messages:
jana: Hey docs — customers hit a weird NAT hairpinning case in Private quickstart when the installer talks to an on-host KMS behind a cloud NAT. Can we add a short troubleshooting note and a tiny Node.js SDK example showing tcp vs unix KMS transport?

omar: I can add the troubleshooting note and anchor alias. I'll mention double-NAT and recommend forcing `hostNetwork` or using a reachable TCP endpoint when in clouds that do SNAT hairpinning.

li: Suggested runnable snippets:
```bash
# nftables minimal postrouting masquerade (sealed site)
nft add table ip nat
nft 'add chain ip nat POSTROUTING { type nat hook postrouting priority 100; }'
nft add rule ip nat POSTROUTING oifname "eth0" masquerade
# iptables fallback
iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -o eth0 -j MASQUERADE
```
And a compact Node.js example for docs:
```js
// node example: select KMS transport at client init
const {Client} = require('redwood-sdk');
// unix socket (air-gapped)
const c1 = new Client({kmsTransport: 'unix', kmsSocket: '/var/run/kms.sock'});
// tcp (remote KMS)
const c2 = new Client({kmsTransport: 'tcp', kmsHost: 'kms.internal', kmsPort: 443});
```
Also add a one-line systemd ExecStartPre to ensure pkcs11 socket perms: `ExecStartPre=/bin/chown redwood-installer:installer /var/run/pkcs11.sock && /bin/chmod 660 /var/run/pkcs11.sock`
